ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law, transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 instituting the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended, with public access curtailed as a consequence of the Court of Justice of the European Union judgments of 22 November 2022, joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (LSC), including Article 4-1 and the SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the practical arrangements of the Register of Beneficial Owners; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on anti-money laundering, as amended, and CSSF AML/CFT Circular 18/698; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 12 December 2019 implementing Union and international financial sanctions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil status, passport or national identity authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-EU documents; notarized certified copy accepted within the EU e-CODEX framework

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of registration, statutory excerpt and current articles of association of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register or trade registry in the corporate general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (where the issuing state is not a Hague Convention contracting party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and certificate of current officers, directors and authorised signatories of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry, Chamber of Commerce or governmental authority of the general partner's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate and proof of no adverse tax or insolvency record of the general partner and of any limited partner upon individual request
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority and insolvency registry of the partner's state of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and financial-standing / AML KYC package issued to the corporate general partner by its home bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank or licensed financial institution of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarised bank letterhead certification with apostille or consular legalization if expressly demanded by the receiving Luxembourg fiduciary or depositary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg formation agent, notary and registered-office provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The partners or the corporate general partner, executed before a notary or with legalised signatures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for foreign signatories

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, ultimate beneficial owners, authorised signatories and the corporate general partner's directors and officers against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC SDN List (where a US nexus exists), the United Kingdom HM Treasury consolidated list (where a UK nexus exists), and the FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdiction statements. PEP status is determined under Article 1(1)(12) of the AML/CFT Law, covering persons resident or exercising public functions outside Luxembourg, with additional domestic PEP checks against Luxembourg public-office holders; enhanced due diligence is engaged for PEPs, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation. Hits not cleared by documentation or independent determination are resolved by the compliance officer and, where the suspicion threshold is met, a report is filed with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier, CRF) under Articles 6 and 10 to 12 of the AML/CFT Law. Continuous sanctions and adverse-media screening is required during the entire business relationship; refusal to deal applies where a screening hit remains unresolved.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online platform, RCS module, available at https://www.lbr.lu (formerly MyRCS; operated by the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be written in the Latin alphabet and may be expressed in French, German or English, or a combination of these working languages; proposed names originally articulated in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese or Cyrillic characters) must be submitted with a certified phonetic or literal transliteration into Latin script. The name must end with the legal form indicator 'SCSp' or the full wording 'société en commandite spéciale', and must not be confusingly similar to any denomination already registered in Luxembourg or misleading as to the legal nature of the entity. RCS notices are issued in French; supporting constitutional documents in German or English may require a certified French translation where the registrar so requests.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation at the Luxembourg Business Registers is valid for 30 days and cannot be extended administratively; the applicant may submit a fresh reservation with the same denomination on the day after expiry or earlier with a slightly adjusted denomination, provided no identical or confusingly similar name has since been reserved or registered. Upon formal rejection by the RCS registrar, the applicant or its registered formation agent must lodge a written reasoned objection with the RCS within 15 days of the electronic notification; the RCS is required to re-examine the objection and issue a new decision. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may appeal to the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within one month of the final administrative rejection, supported by evidence of prior use, registered trademark rights, distinctive character and the absence of a risk of confusion; a further appeal on points of law lies to the Cour d'appel. Expedited judicial interim relief is available where the rejected name is indispensable to a signed acquisition or operational lease agreement.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the statutory seat of an SCSp only where a licensed Luxembourg registered-office provider accepts domiciliation at its own physical premises; the SCSp must otherwise be reachable at the registered office for court summons, tax correspondence and AML/CFT supervision. For an operating ISIC 5210 refrigerated logistics business storing perishable pharmaceuticals, virtual office arrangements are commercially insufficient: the entity must obtain and maintain physical custody of, or lease, a suitable cold-storage facility subject to Good Distribution Practices (GDP) licensing under Directive 2001/83/EC and EU Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/161, with temperature monitoring, qualified-person oversight, qualified personnel and insurable stock; moreover, if Luxembourg tax residence is claimed for the pass-through partnership, effective central management and business conduct must demonstrably take place in Luxembourg. Virtual office use is therefore limited to ancillary administrative purposes and cannot satisfy commercial-substance or GDP requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 77% central expectation of at least one unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months following grant of the Luxembourg wholesale distribution authorisation and GDP certification; unannounced inspections are the standard methodology under EU GDP inspection coordination, and temperature-controlled pharmaceutical storage consistently ranks in the high-priority inspection bracket.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SCSp formation of EUR 2,000-3,500, excluding VAT and disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarisation of the partnership agreement and related corporate resolutions (optional at incorporation stage unless real estate is contributed; here recommended for bank KYC acceptance)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff schedule for acts without calculable monetary object plus notary attendance and registry disbursements; market rate for authentication of a standard SCSp deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS commercial register filing and publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) / Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS and RESA publication tariffs approximating EUR 8-20 for fully digital filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner (RBE) registration filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers through the appointed registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE module) and appointed registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Platform tariff for direct e-filing is free; agent filing fee of EUR 100-150 is the prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; specifically Articles 70-71-4 on the special limited partnership (société en commandite spéciale, SCSp), introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; Registry filing provisions of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and the amended Law of 30 September 2022 on establishment of commercial activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: RCS Form A – Request for insertion in the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies, together with the executed partnership agreement and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital requirement for an SCSp; no mandatory paid-up capital or escrow account requirement. Contributions may be in cash or in kind, and may be payable at the dates fixed in the partnership agreement. Limited partner liability is contractually capped at the contribution, whereas the general partner is liable without limit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) in Luxembourg be, and is hereby, approved in accordance with the executed partnership agreement which sets forth the issuance and acceptance of all partnership interests, including the general partner's unlimited interest and the special partner's restricted interest. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the SCSp be established at the street address specified in the formation documents and that the general partner is authorised to conclude any lease or service agreement in respect thereof. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be, and hereby is, appointed as manager (gérant) of the SCSp with full power to represent the partnership, to open bank accounts, and to effect all statutory filings. This resolution is effective upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of SCSp Partnership Agreement and Subscription of Partnership Interests
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Duly appointed Luxembourg notary (mandatory if real estate or a legal form of real right is contributed; otherwise private deed is sufficient) or the partners directly
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in English, French, or German, indicating the unlimited general partner and the limited special partner(s), their capital subscription, profit sharing, and management powers. Execute by all partners; if notarial form is required, sign before a Luxembourg notary. Retain the executed deed for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Statement of in-cash or in-kind contributions
Legal entity identifiers (LEI) of corporate partners, if applicable
Proof of address and AML/KYC documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a contribution of real estate occurs without the mandatory notarial form, the deed may be attacked for nullity; cure by executing a corrective notarial deed before filing with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File RCS Form A through the official RCS e-File system, attaching the executed partnership agreement, identification of the manager, and proof of the registered office. The registration makes the SCSp a distinct legal entity and issues the RCS number.
required_dossiers: Identification of the manager/gérant and signed acceptance of office
Criminal record certificate (bulletin n°3) of the manager
Proof of registered office (lease agreement or owner's consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a rejection or query, file a supplementary declaration within 15 calendar days, correct all identified omissions, and pay any supplemental fee; specific missing annexes can be cured by separate online attachments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Formation Instruments in the Electronic Official Gazette RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal Information Service of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, transmit the registration extract and the partnership agreement to the RESA service for publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations. Publication provides third-party opposability of the formation and manager powers.
required_dossiers: Copy of the RCS registration extract
Original or notarized copy of the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is refused or flagged, submit a corrected version within five working days; the publication date is effective only after a fully compliant notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Establishment Authorisation for Cold Storage Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy, General Directorate for SMEs and Entrepreneurship
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for an establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) in accordance with the Law of 30 September 2022 on the establishment and exercise of commercial activities. Provide proof of the eligible manager and of the operating site. The permit grants the right to pursue the refrigerated warehousing business.
required_dossiers: Description of cold storage premises and intended operations
Criminal record certificate of the statutory manager
Evidence of professional competence of the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Ministry of the Economy within one month; request an administrative hearing and submit missing documentation to cure the grounds for refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Good Distribution Practice / Wholesale Distribution Licence for Pharmaceutical Cold-Chain Warehousing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Health, Direction de la Santé – Division of Pharmacy and Medicines
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for wholesale distribution authorisation for medicinal products under Luxembourg law implementing Directive 2001/83/EC and EU Good Distribution Practice rules. Demonstrate validated temperature-controlled storage, alarm systems, contingency plans, and qualified-person supervision.
required_dossiers: Good Distribution Practice policies and SOPs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry issues observations, provide a written corrective action plan within ten working days and coordinate an inspector visit; any negative decision can be appealed through the administrative appeal process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Notification and EIA Screening for Classified Installation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Environnement – Luxembourg Environment Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notify the operation as an établissement classé under the Law of 9 May 2014 on the environment. Submit data on refrigerant quantities (F-gases, ammonia), cooling and wastewater discharges, noise, and traffic. If the project exceeds EIA thresholds, submit a full or preliminary environmental impact study.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Administration requires a full EIA or an operating permit, file the relevant impact study within the deadline; negative decisions may be appealed to the Minister within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp with AEDT using the RCS extract and partnership agreement to obtain the Luxembourg VAT number and a direct corporate tax file. If employees are hired, register with CCSS for social security. Also arrange for annual accounts to be filed with RCS.
required_dossiers: Employment declarations, if any employees will be hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT or CCSS returns a query, correct the online registration and resubmit omitted documents; late registrations can be cured by filing a late-registration notice and paying the statutory late fee as invoiced.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health, Direction de la Santé – Division of Pharmacy and Medicines (GDP licence) in conjunction with the Ministry of the Economy (establishment authorisation)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation de distribution en gros des médicaments – Wholesale Distribution and Good Distribution Practice (GDP) Operating Licence for Temperature-Controlled Pharmaceutical Cold Storage Warehouses

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Luxembourg Environment Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified installation under the Luxembourg Law of 9 May 2014 – Registration/Tier B for typical cold storage warehouses; a full EIA report is required only where quantities of refrigerants, hazardous substances, or waste exceed the thresholds of Annexes I and II of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 September 1995 on wastewater and industrial discharge; F-gas leakage must be managed under EU Regulation 517/2014 with mandatory annual leak checks for systems above 5 tCO2e; VOC emissions, if applicable, must remain below EU Directive 1999/13/EC limits; industrial noise at the facility boundary must not exceed 65 dB(A) daytime and 55 dB(A) night-time; refrigerants with high GWP must be substituted where technically feasible.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The facility must obtain fire safety approval from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS), including fire alarm and sprinkler commissioning; a structural-load and building-safety certificate from a certified civil engineer; and an occupational safety approval from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including evacuation plans, cold-room emergency locking prevention, and refrigerant gas detection systems.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified digital filing via MyGuichet.lu / RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Apply for inclusion in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through an approved filing intermediary, obtaining a national business number (Numéro d'identification). Use that number to file a VAT registration application with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu; the VAT number is issued immediately in the format LU00000000. The SCSp itself is not subject to corporate income tax and no CIT ID is required; the partners are taxed directly. If the SCSp elects to be treated as a taxable corporation under LIR Article 5 bis, a separate CIT tax file must be activated with the ACD.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SCSp is fiscally transparent by default. Pursuant to LIR Article 5 bis, an SCSp may elect irrevocably to be treated as a body corporate for direct tax purposes if all its partners are corporate taxpayers; this election is exercised in the annual corporate return. No check-the-box regime exists. For indirect tax, no election affects VAT status; the SCSp is a separate taxable person for VAT purposes when it carries on an economic activity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Act (loi modifiée du 12 février 1979)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for the small-business exemption; registration is compulsory once the SCSp's taxable supplies in Luxembourg exceed this threshold. Non-established foreign entities supplying services in Luxembourg under the general B2B place-of-supply rule do not benefit from the threshold and must register unless the reverse charge applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping. For B2G supplies, electronic invoicing through PEPPOL BIS is mandatory. B2B e-invoicing is optional and governed by private contract; common formats are ZUGFeRD/FACTUR-X and UBL. EU ViDA proposals may introduce sector-specific e-invoicing obligations after 2028, which the SCSp should monitor.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For cold-storage warehousing services supplied by the Luxembourg SCSp to a taxable customer established outside the EU, the place of supply is outside Luxembourg and the supply is outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT, resulting in a 0% effective charge (not a statutory exemption). Where the SCSp itself physically exports goods from a customs warehouse to a non-EU destination, the goods supply is zero-rated under the export exemption; related storage and handling services can qualify as ancillary export services if performed directly in connection with fully-completed exports and the services' value is supported by prescribed evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/EAD) filed via the LLMAM e-Douane system and validated with MRN
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill/CMR consignment note
Commercial invoice showing 0% VAT and, where available, the customer's non-EU VAT number or equivalent proof of taxable status
Bank Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing actual forex receipt from the non-EU customer
Warehouse movement/issue records and temperature-log evidence substantiating physical investigation by customs authorities
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Wrongful zero-rating or unfounded export claims subject the SCSp to retrospective VAT collection with statutory late interest (currently 0.88% per month in arrears), administrative fines up to 100% of the evaded tax under Article 55(13) TVA, and criminal liability in cases of deliberate fraud (fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment). Supporting documentation must be retained for at least 6 years for VAT purposes and 10 years for customs purposes; incomplete documentation triggers automatic clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). No separate foreign exchange administration body exists; the BCL performs monetary policy and balance-of-payments statistical functions, while the CSSF supervises banks and payment institutions for AML/KYC and prudential matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Free and full convertibility. Luxembourg is a Eurozone member; Article 63 TFEU prohibits all restrictions on capital movements and payments between Member States and third countries. The capital and current accounts are completely liberalized: profit remittances, dividends, interest, and liquidation proceeds may be freely transferred without prior administrative authorization or central bank approval. Foreign-currency accounts are permitted and may be converted to EUR at market rates. The only practical requirements are statutory bank reporting of balance-of-payments statistics under BCL regulations (including a purpose code on each transfer) and verification of the economic substance of the transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no obligatory surrender of export proceeds, no repatriation deadlines, and no mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts. Exporters and trading entities may retain receivables in any convertible currency and time their conversion freely. Generic EU payment transparency duties under Regulation (EU) 2015/847 (originator and beneficiary information) apply to all cross-border transfers, but these are informational and not exchange-control constraints.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / FX and Cash-Pooling Account
Operational Account / Trade Finance Account (LC and Guarantees)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for low-value SEPA collections and disbursement automation; Low for capital custody and large trade settlements. Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions and payment institutions (e.g., Banking Circle S.A., Mangopay) are supervised by the CSSF under the PSD2 regime and the 2009 e-money and payment services laws, and can provide multi-currency IBANs. However, subscription capital for an SCSp and substantial cross-border supplier payments should remain in a tier-1 commercial bank, because EMIs typically decline partnership structures with non-resident UBOs, lack depositary-grade escrow, and are not designated counterparties for BCL statistical reporting in the same manner as credit institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for an SCSp, particularly when the General Partner is foreign-managed. Luxembourg banks normally demand an in-person KYC interview at the branch with the authorised signatories of the General Partner; remote video-identification is accepted only for simple low-risk corporate clients and is rarely applied to partnership vehicles with non-resident investors. At minimum, one General Partner representative must appear physically and bring original corporate documents; the bank may additionally require a local professional intermediary (exchange lawyer, notary, or domiciliation agent) to co-sign the opening mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO look-through of a multi-tier SCSp: investors in offshore feeders (Cayman, BVI, Delaware) hold more than 25% of capital or control, and the beneficial owners cannot be immediately traced to natural persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised organisational chart with complete look-through; limited partnership agreement (LPA); subscription register; Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RCBE) extract naming the natural-person UBOs; sworn declaration by the General Partner; CSSF or AIFM authorisation if the vehicle is an AIF; independent counsel opinion confirming the control chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp incorporated without legal personality (common in fund structures), creating ambiguity as to counterparty standing, asset ownership, and account-title eligibility.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement executed under the Luxembourg Law of 12 July 2013 and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended); express election clause confirming absence of legal personality; Commercial Register (RCS) excerpt; General Partner resolution authorising account opening with specimen signatures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds: large inbound capital injections from a non-EU parent or group treasury, leading the bank to question provenance and economic substance of the cold-storage entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the contributing entity; intercompany loan or equity subscription agreements; purchase invoices and SPAs for the temperature-controlled assets; 12 months of upstream bank statements; tax residence certificates; detailed business plan for ISIC 5210/NAICS 493120 refrigerated logistics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hit on an indirect beneficial owner, General Partner, or major counterparty, including Russia/Belarus restrictions or OFAC SDN matches.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Risk-based due diligence file satisfying CSSF Regulation 12-02; PEP and sanctions declaration under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019; notarised source-of-wealth report; screening results with narrative explanation of any alias or address mismatch; independent legal opinion confirming absence of designated persons and no evasion schemes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulated business scope: temperature-controlled cold storage for pharmaceutical products triggers health and good-distribution-practice checks, which the bank must assess as reputational and compliance risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg Ministry of Health or food-chain safety authorisation under the Law of 17 August 2018; HACCP certification; EU Good Distribution Practice (GDP) certificate for pharma handling; statutory operating licence for ISIC 5210; documented storage temperature and monitoring protocols; the bank's AML risk tier remains classified as 'Low_Risk_Standard'.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For euro transfers from within the EU/EEA: SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) via any EU bank, using purpose code EQUI (equity capital injection) or CFDI (capital foreign direct investment). For non-euro or extra-SEPA transfers: SWIFT MT103 with Field 50K (ordering customer), Field 57A (Luxembourg beneficiary bank, e.g., BIL or BCEE), and Field 70 containing the BCL balance-of-payments statistical purpose code for direct investment plus the reference to the LPA and capital call notice. Verification pack: GP capital call resolution, investor subscription form, RCBE extract, and proof of economic substance; no exchange-control permit is required. Beneficiary account must be labelled 'SCSp — Capital Escrow Account' and segregated from operating funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Eurozone suppliers: SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Direct Debit (pain.001/pain.008) for utilities, rent, payroll, and low-value logistics expenses. Non-euro suppliers: SWIFT MT103 with purpose code INTC or TRAD, using correspondent clearing through T2 (the Eurosystem large-value payment system, successor to TARGET2) for euro legs, CHIPS/Fedwire for USD legs, and CHAPS for GBP legs; MT202 COV for cover payments. For pharma cold-chain goods and capital equipment: Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600, optionally Bank Payment Obligations (URBPO) on the SWIFT trade platform. All disbursements must reference the relevant invoice and be executed exclusively from the Operational Account, never from the Capital Escrow Account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD FX outright forwards and currency swaps (OTC with any EU bank; no exchange-traded mandate; SCSp has full legal capacity to hedge commercial exposures)
EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF forward contracts and FX swaps under ISDA 2002 or local master agreements

Cross-currency basis swaps (EUR/USD) to synthetically convert injected foreign-currency capital into euro, subject to EMIR reporting and, if applicable, mandatory clearing thresholds (clearing threshold for FX and interest-rate OTC derivatives is EUR 3 billion gross notional; small financial counterparty exemption may apply)
Purchased and written FX options for tenant contracts and energy-price-linked revenue; options are permissible under Luxembourg law and do not alter the partnership's pass-through tax treatment

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for restricted-currency receivables arising from clients in jurisdictions such as CNY, INR, KRW, or BRL; NDFs on EUR are neither available nor necessary because the euro is fully convertible
Same-day FX spot transactions for operational and payroll flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS Confirmation (Reconduction annuelle de l'inscription au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the anniversary date of RCS registration; filing must be made electronically during the month of the anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers default penalties based on LBR enforcement rules; repeated failure to confirm RCS data may result in administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and court-ordered strike-off of the RCS registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs – confirmation annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the anniversary of RCS registration, or within one month of any change in beneficial ownership for mandatory interim updates, whichever is earlier.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or keep UBO data accurate constitutes an AML/CTF breach punishable by criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment of responsible managers under the Luxembourg law of 13 January 2019; repeated non-compliance may also trigger RCS strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Dépôt des comptes annuels) – only if the SCSp has opted for legal personality and is not exempt under thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the closing of the financial year (balance sheet date); smaller entities may benefit from simplified presentation but must still file within the same statutory deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SCSp to administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 per delayed return, manager liability against creditors, and possible court-ordered strike-off after formal default notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory audit applies if the SCSp has legal personality and exceeds two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4m, net turnover EUR 8.8m, average workforce 50 employees; a fully transparent SCSp that has not opted for legal personality is ordinarily exempt from entity-level audit, but managers must ensure partners' tax computations are supported by accurate financial records.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Référentiel comptable luxembourgeois) transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; consolidated or listed entities may apply IFRS as adopted by the EU if required or elected.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must confirm annually, through the LBR electronic portal, the identity, nationality, ownership stakes and nature of control of all ultimate beneficial owners; the confirmation is due within the month of the RCS registration anniversary. Any transfer of partnership interests or change in control must be filed within one month of the event, and the annual confirmation must reflect the final state as of the confirmation date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,200 – 6,500 per annum (EUR 2,000 – 6,000) for professional registered office and corporate agent services in Luxembourg.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,500 – 18,000 for a mandatory statutory audit; USD 2,000 – 5,000 for a voluntary review/due diligence package; transparent SCSp without legal personality typically incurs USD 0 entity-level audit fee.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined Luxembourg City rate comprising 17% national corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge on corporate income tax, and 6.75% municipal business tax; municipal component varies by commune
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% IP-Box exemption on qualifying net IP income (effective rate circa 5.2% in Luxembourg City); 100% participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital gain income; 1% EU/EEA parent-subsidiary dividend withholding rate; R&D tax credit for warehouse automation and logistics software; no capital duty on SCSp capital contributions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 (Déclaration annuelle pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune) e-filed through MyGuichet.lu, the official Luxembourg e-administration portal; the fiscally transparent SCSp attaches a partnership allocation schedule reporting each partner's distributable share
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return aligned to the fiscal year, which defaults to the calendar year; assessed corporate income tax is payable after assessment, and advance payments are due quarterly for assessments exceeding statutory thresholds
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the year following the fiscal year end for calendar-year accounts; within five months after fiscal year closure for non-calendar year ends; extensions of one to three months may be granted on reasoned application to the Administration des contributions directes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification particulars: entity name, corporate seat, RBE beneficial ownership registration number, VAT identification number, and fiscal representative details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners without a Luxembourg permanent establishment are not required to file; where a permanent establishment exists, the SCSp or its local tax representative files and attaches the partner's Tax Residence Certificate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable commercial result: turnover from temperature-controlled storage, warehouse rental and handling revenue, cost of goods sold, energy and refrigeration costs, depreciation, salaries, and provisions of the refrigerated logistics business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only income and expenses effectively connected with the Luxembourg permanent establishment must be declared; non-resident limited partners include only their distributive share of Luxembourg-source PE income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses under Article 45 LIR: income-based taxes, excessive gifts, fines, and remuneration paid under undisclosed or non-arm's length arrangements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers must add back the same items attributable to the Luxembourg PE; intercompany service fees failing the Article 56 LIR arm's length standard are re-included

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption and IP-Box elections: dividends and capital gains under Articles 166 and 166bis LIR, and 80% net IP income exemption under Article 50bis LIR
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty-protected capital gains and participation relief require documented proof of beneficial ownership, qualifying holding percentage, and 12-month holding period; GAAR and treaty abuse defences apply

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and prepayments: foreign tax credits, Luxembourg withholding tax credits, R&D tax credit, and quarterly advance payments imputed against the final assessment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may credit Luxembourg PE tax against home-country tax only to the extent granted by the applicable DTA; refunds of excess prepayments require a Luxembourg bank account and tax representative

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplemental schedules: balance sheet, profit and loss account, depreciation ledger, transfer pricing Local File and Master File declarations, and Country-by-Country Report notification where applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing documentation thresholds apply to the whole group; the ACD may require production of the transfer pricing file within 30 days, and documentation may be submitted in French, German, or English

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a statutory late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax (minimum EUR 30), coercive fines up to EUR 25,000 for continued non-compliance, and late-payment interest at 0.5% per commenced month; negligent misdeclaration attracts surcharges up to 15% of the reassessed tax, and fraudulent evasion is criminally prosecuted with fines up to EUR 75,000 and imprisonment up to five years

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; reduced to 1% for dividends paid to a qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of the share capital, alone or jointly, for an uninterrupted 12-month period; DTA rates of 0% to 15% may apply under Luxembourg's treaty network
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The withholding agent may apply the DTA or EU directive rate at source only after receiving: a valid Tax Residence Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, evidence of beneficial ownership, share register and participation records proving the qualifying holding and 12-month holding period, and a signed treaty-relief declaration addressed to the Administration des contributions directes; any excess withholding tax must be recovered through a formal refund claim filed with the ACD within the applicable limitation period, generally three years from the end of the calendar year in which the tax was charged
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax of 0% on outgoing interest and 0% on outgoing royalties; Luxembourg does not impose source withholding taxes on interest or IP royalties, so treaty reduced rates are not required at payment; thin capitalisation, back-to-back royalties, and hybrid mismatch arrangements remain subject to Article 56 LIR, ATAD interest limitation rules, and beneficial ownership scrutiny

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are mandatory where the Luxembourg entity belongs to a group with consolidated net turnover equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000,000 and intragroup purchases or provisions of goods and services exceed EUR 250,000 during the tax year; Country-by-Country Report filing applies to groups with consolidated revenue equal to or exceeding EUR 750,000,000
